items.title: Fireworks Research launches Ember-1, a specialized AI model delivering Kimi K3 quality with 40% fewer tokens for efficient coding and reasoning [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Fireworks Research introduced Ember-1, a new AI model built on Kimi K3 that reduces token usage by 40% while maintaining answer quality. Ember-1 was developed to address the high cost of long reasoning traces in automated coding, achieving more efficient reasoning through extensive training and new algorithms. The model was tested across multiple benchmarks, live customer A/B tests, and internal workloads, confirming consistent quality with fewer tokens. Ember-1 represents the first in a series of specialized models from Fireworks Research, designed to meet developer needs and built using the Fireworks Serverless Training platform without using customer data.

items.title: TinyAIArena launches platform for AI agents to compete against each other in simulated battles [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: TinyAIArena has introduced a platform where AI agents can battle each other in a controlled environment. The site allows users to watch AI agents compete, showcasing different strategies and behaviors in real time. This platform provides a space for experimenting with AI interactions and observing emergent behaviors in agent competitions.

items.title: George Hotz says AI coding tools have disrupted traditional hiring bounties at tinygrad, urging candidates to contribute directly to the open-source project [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: George Hotz, founder of tinygrad, explained that AI tools like Claude Code have undermined the effectiveness of traditional bounty programs for hiring by enabling superficial contributions. He encourages prospective hires to engage directly with tinygrad's public development process through Discord and GitHub, focusing on deep bug fixes and thoughtful improvements rather than feature additions. Hotz emphasizes that AI has not changed the core hiring criteria and that the project aims to challenge big tech's infrastructure dominance over a long-term horizon. The role offers a flexible hybrid work environment with a weekly meeting and biweekly sprint summaries, paying $75k-$150k plus equity.

items.title: WSJ examines why AI excels at complex math problems but struggles to fully solve chess
items.content_text: Artificial intelligence has made significant breakthroughs in solving some of the most challenging problems in mathematics, yet it has not achieved a definitive solution to chess. The article explores the reasons behind this discrepancy, highlighting the unique complexities and strategic depth of chess that continue to challenge AI systems. It discusses the differences in problem structure between mathematical puzzles and chess, as well as the limitations of current AI approaches in fully mastering the game.

items.title: Governments struggle to keep pace with rapid AI advancements, raising concerns about regulation and societal impact management [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Governments worldwide are falling behind as artificial intelligence technology advances rapidly, creating challenges in adapting policies and regulations to manage AI's societal effects effectively. This lag raises concerns about public institutions' ability to harness AI's benefits while mitigating risks. The widening gap between AI development and government oversight highlights the need for more agile and informed approaches to AI governance.

items.title: NAND-16: a computer constructed from 277,248 NAND gates
items.content_text: NAND-16 is a computer built entirely from 277,248 NAND gates, demonstrating a large-scale implementation of basic logic components. This project showcases the construction of a functional computing system using only NAND gates, highlighting the fundamental role of this logic gate in digital electronics.

items.title: Harvard and MIT Press release two-volume Machine Learning Systems textbook covering AI engineering from single machines to fleet-scale infrastructure [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Harvard University and MIT Press have published a two-volume textbook titled Machine Learning Systems, offering a rigorous, principles-first approach to building, optimizing, and deploying machine learning systems at various scales. The curriculum includes interactive labs, a framework-building toolkit, performance modeling tools, hardware deployment kits, and teaching resources aimed at students, instructors, and professionals. The project supports a comprehensive AI engineering education with materials such as lecture slides, interview practice questions, and a full course blueprint. It is actively maintained and freely accessible online, targeting a global audience with the goal of training one million AI engineers by 2030.

items.title: Flavio Copes argues fundamentals remain essential for developers despite AI-generated code
items.content_text: Flavio Copes discusses the continued importance of learning programming fundamentals even as AI tools increasingly write code. He emphasizes that understanding core concepts helps developers effectively use AI-generated code and maintain control over software quality. The article highlights that foundational knowledge remains critical for debugging, customization, and long-term career growth in an AI-assisted coding environment.

items.title: Oura plans IPO amid strong revenue growth but faces skepticism due to single-product subscription model risks
items.content_text: Oura, a fitness ring maker, is expected to go public despite concerns about its business model. The company reported revenue of $907.9 million in fiscal 2025, more than doubling from the previous year, and generated $100 million in cash during the same period. However, analysts note similarities to other single-product subscription companies like Peloton, GoPro, and Fitbit, which have struggled after their IPOs. This raises questions about Oura's long-term sustainability despite its recent financial performance.

items.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to dine with President Trump at the White House, marking their first meeting
items.content_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is scheduled to have a private dinner with President Donald Trump at the White House on Sunday, marking their first meeting. This event could indicate a potential warming of relations between Anthropic and the Trump administration.

items.title: Bill Gates says Donald Trump is wrong to oppose AI safeguards amid growing concerns over artificial intelligence risks
items.content_text: Bill Gates criticized former President Donald Trump's stance against implementing safeguards for artificial intelligence, arguing that such protections are necessary as AI technologies advance. Gates emphasized the importance of regulation to manage potential risks associated with AI development and deployment. This disagreement highlights ongoing debates among prominent figures about how best to balance innovation with safety in the rapidly evolving AI landscape.

items.title: Simon Willison reviews 2026 advancements in large language models, coding agents, AI security incidents, and AI's societal impact [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: In 2026, large language models like Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 reached new reliability in coding agents, enabling daily use and sparking widespread developer experimentation. Personal AI agents, known as "Claws," gained popularity, especially in China, alongside efforts to create safer versions for general users. Open-weight models capable of running on laptops showed significant improvements, while security breaches involving rogue AI agents on platforms like Hugging Face and RubyGems prompted government interventions and export controls in the US. Anthropic's Claude Mythos faced restrictions due to hacking capabilities, and the Pope issued an encyclical addressing AI's impact on humanity. The year also highlighted ongoing challenges in AI safety and deployment, with notable progress in sandboxing and agent security discussed at industry conferences. Additionally, the endangered New Zealand Kākāpō parrot experienced a significant breeding season, marking a rare positive environmental event amid rapid AI developments.

items.title: WSJ outlines indicators that could signal an impending bust in the AI investment boom [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The article examines signs that may indicate a downturn in the current surge of interest and investment in artificial intelligence technologies. It discusses factors such as market saturation, waning investor enthusiasm, and technological challenges that could lead to a slowdown or bust in the AI industry.

items.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to have first one-on-one dinner with President Trump amid AI safety debate [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is scheduled to have a one-on-one dinner with President Donald Trump at the White House, marking their first private meeting. The two have recently been on opposing sides of the AI safety discussion, with Amodei advocating for cautious AI development and Trump dismissing AI concerns as a political hoax while promoting the term "super intelligence." Amodei and Anthropic have also faced challenges with the Trump administration, including a Pentagon designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk, which the company is contesting in court.

items.title: Meta launches Muse AI agent with consumer focus amid skepticism over trust and ongoing usage [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Meta introduced Muse, a new AI agent showcased at its annual Connect event, aiming to embed AI features into consumer products rather than enterprise tools. The launch contrasts with competitors like OpenAI and Anthropic, which are focusing on enterprise applications and monetization strategies. While Muse offers features such as finding unclaimed funds, early impressions describe it as more of a novelty than a tool for sustained use. Concerns remain about user trust given Meta's advertising-driven business model, raising questions about how comfortable users will be sharing sensitive information with the AI agent. The company's consumer-centric approach leverages its established presence in everyday social apps, but its success depends on overcoming these trust issues and proving ongoing value to users.

items.title: Thoughtful Things launches Engram, an AI-powered sampler that transforms audio with local tiny AI models for experimental music creation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Thoughtful Things has launched a Kickstarter campaign for Engram, its first instrument that uses AI to manipulate incoming audio and generate new sounds. Unlike typical AI music tools, Engram runs a custom-trained, locally operating tiny AI model and focuses on experimental sound design rather than producing polished songs. The device is designed as a "field recorder for latent space," allowing users to explore AI hallucinations and circuit-bend the AI models for unique audio effects. Engram's firmware will be open for customization, and the Kickstarter offers a limited run starting at $675, with expected retail pricing between $850 and $900.

items.title: llama.cpp speeds up prompt lookup drafting by up to 42x with memory optimizations, achieving up to 140x speedup including external contributions [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A developer improved prompt lookup decoding in llama.cpp, making it up to 42 times faster and reducing memory usage by up to 2.6 times through performance optimizations inspired by prior research. An additional contribution from Daniel Lemire further accelerated the process, bringing the total speedup to approximately 140 times. Prompt lookup decoding in llama.cpp uses n-gram caches to predict the next tokens during model inference, combining context, dynamic, and static caches with configurable thresholds to draft tokens efficiently. These enhancements benefit popular inference engines and machine learning libraries that implement similar speculative decoding techniques.

items.title: OliverDB outperforms ClickHouse by over 2.8× on 244 query types in benchmarks with 50 million rows on AWS bare-metal servers
items.content_text: OliverDB conducted benchmarks comparing its database engine to ClickHouse using 244 query shapes on 50 million rows loaded from the same data generator on AWS bare-metal servers. OliverDB completed all queries in less than half the total time ClickHouse took, including data loading, and outperformed ClickHouse across all query families tested. The largest speedup was a 290× improvement on a common user event count query, achieved by reading significantly fewer rows due to compact data summaries and pre-computed aggregates. The tests were repeated four times over three weeks with consistent results showing OliverDB's median speedup between 2.84× and 3.06×. OliverDB's engine compiles queries into programs that optimize filter and aggregation execution in a single data pass. The same engine powers OliverDB Cloud and can be deployed on private cloud accounts, supporting existing SQL workloads and JSON data ingestion.

items.title: China Weighs Allowing Purchases of New Nvidia Chips by ByteDance, Alibaba [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: China's government has signaled it could allow some domestic companies to buy a new Nvidia chip built for high-end professional computers, according to two people familiar with the matter, as the country's AI firms strain for enough computing power to run their chatbots and agents. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, which oversees China's tech sector, recently asked companies including Alibaba Group and ByteDance to report on their plans to buy Nvidia's RTX Pro 5500 chips, released this month-specifically how many they want to buy and what they'll use them for, the people said. The ministry has told some Chinese companies the government intends to approve the purchases, they said. Even if that happens, though, it's unclear when the approvals would come, how many chips officials would allow and what standards they would use to decide.

items.title: Kākāpō Party [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Tool: Kākāpō Party I presented a closing keynote for the WeAreDevelopers World Congress North America yesterday. As a STAR moment I decided to weave in references to the record breaking kākāpō breeding season we had in 2026. For my closing slide I wanted to celebrate, and I had seen some buzz around how good Claude Opus 5.5 was at creating pixel art animations. So I rounded up three Kakapo photos from Google image search and dropped them into Claude with this prompt: Here are some photos of kakapo parrots just to remind you what they look like I need you to make an animation in animated pixel art on HTML 5 canvas of obviously pixel art kakapo jumping up and down having a party with confetti and suchlike - there should be at least 20 of them Here's the transcript, and this is the resulting page. It's pretty great! I wanted to embed it in a Keynote presentation file, so I downloaded the HTML and told a local Claude Code session: Make me a video of file:///Users/simon/Downloads/kakapo-party.html - you need to load it in a browser and click on it a few times to get the confetti effect, the video should be 15s long don't start clicking until 3s in make sure several clicks are spread around the clickable area Claude Code used Playwright (transcript here) and produced this video, which was exactly what I needed for my final slide: Your browser does not support HTML5 video. Here's the full Playwright script it used, which was pleasingly short: # /// script # dependencies = ["playwright"] # /// import time from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright W, H = 1280, 720 # Canvas fills the viewport; spread clicks across corners, edges and centre clicks = [ (3.0, 640, 360), # centre (4.2, 160, 120), # top-left (5.4, 1120, 120), # top-right (6.6, 180, 600), # bottom-left (7.8, 1100, 600), # bottom-right (9.0, 640, 100), # top-centre (10.0, 380, 380), # mid-left (11.0, 900, 380), # mid-right (12.2, 640, 620), # bottom-centre (13.2, 640, 300), # finale centre ] with sync_playwright() as p: b = p.chromium.launch() ctx = b.new_context(viewport={"width":W,"height":H}, record_video_dir="vids", record_video_size={"width":W,"height":H}) page = ctx.new_page() t0 = time.time() page.goto("file:///Users/simon/Downloads/kakapo-party.html") for t,x,y in clicks: time.sleep(max(0, t-(time.time()-t0))) page.mouse.click(x,y) time.sleep(max(0, 16.0-(time.time()-t0))) ctx.close(); b.close() Tags: animation, speaking, ai, kakapo, playwright, generative-ai, llms, anthropic, claude, claude-code
